title: Australian Education Amendment (School Funding Guarantee) Bill 2014
short_title: Australian Education Amendment (School Funding Guarantee) Bill 2014

speeches.speaker: Kate Ellis
speeches.brief: Accused the coalition of breaking its election promise to match Labor's school funding dollar for dollar, saying this year's budget cuts $30 billion from Australian school funding, the biggest cut in the nation's history, and warned states no longer have to match every $2 of Commonwealth funding with $1 of their own.

speeches.speaker: Julie Owens
speeches.brief: Supported the schools funding bill, noting high school retention rates rose from about 40 per cent to close to 80 per cent under the Hawke-Keating government, and cited $183 million in education cuts and 700 lost positions in Western Australia.

speeches.speaker: Amanda Rishworth
speeches.brief: Supported the Australian Education Amendment (School Funding Guarantee) Bill 2014, arguing the government had broken its commitments on Gonski funding and proposing needs-based funding tied to preventing further state education cuts.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: Opposed the Australian Education Amendment (School Funding Guarantee) Bill 2014, arguing the coalition had restored $1.2 billion and increased Queensland school funding while criticising Labor's spending, debt and education funding model and advocating teacher quality, school autonomy, parental engagement and curriculum reform.
